did: Tested live in the browser pane by hand. The restaurant set "Advance for orders over 500" at 30%. A guest ordered a Family Combo (1,850) for home delivery and placed the order. The restaurant opened its orders, recorded the advance, and confirmed. The guest read the order page at each step.

checks.text: Before ordering the guest is told: "This is a big order. The restaurant asks for an advance of 555.00 before it starts."
After placing, the order page says: "The restaurant needs an advance of 564.00 before it starts cooking." The restaurant sees "Advance: 0.00 / 564.00" and "Confirm" is switched off
After the restaurant records the advance (564 of 564) "Confirm" turns on; confirming starts the cooking timer, and the guest sees "Advance received: 564.00"

notes: Done by hand in the live browser, not by a script.

Small difference found: the figure before ordering (555.00) is 30% of the food only, while the final advance (564.00) is 30% of the food plus the 30 delivery charge. Both are explained on screen, but the two numbers differ.

shots.caption: The guest is told about the advance before ordering
After placing: the restaurant needs an advance before cooking
The restaurant: Advance 0 of 564, Confirm switched off
The guest: cooking has started, advance received
